verdict.rationale: Jules supports mid-task interaction primarily via its browser web app and API — you can send messages to redirect a running agent, approve/redirect plans, and review diffs/PRs (jules-docs-4, jules-docs-6, jules-docs-7, jules-docs-12, jules-docs-17), and one user reports being prompted to give feedback when Jules stalls (jules-comm-3). However there's no first-party editor/terminal takeover UI (only a user-built MCP bridge to dispatch tasks from VS Code, jules-comm-19), and a hands-on complaint notes there is 'no STOP button to quickly get it out of the loop' (jules-comm-14), undercutting smooth redirection. Missing for 10: native editor/terminal takeover interfaces, a documented interrupt/stop mechanism, and independent confirmation that mid-task redirection reliably works across surfaces.
